About me

I had already written an about me but my best friend told me it wasn't enough, so here is this page.

I grew up in San Diego, between Encanto and Grant Hill. I went to church in Logan Heights. I went to elementary school in Golden Hill. Pretty much, I know San Diego well and I love it here.

I'm from a big Mexican family. We love spending time together. Sometimes we will plan a party just to see each other and spend all day together. It's always been clear to me that I am beyond blessed and privileged to have such a beautiful family.

My grandmother used to say "Amar es entregarse." To love is to give yourself over completely.

This project is a combination of some many years of thinking and reading and writing and having unorganized notes and unarticulated feelings. I think I drove several professors crazy trying to explain myself and in turn felt frustrated with the pessimism of an older generation who just didn't get it.

Millennials have always been a special interest of mine, not only because I am one, but because in 2013, when I was 23 years old, Time Magazine released an article titled, "Me Me Me."

For over a decade, Millennials have been the focal point of social commentary. We have affected politics, art, the economy, culture -- and they won't let us forget it.

Generations older group anyone younger under the label. Generations younger than us reject the label. The difference between the two is that younger generations are experiencing the world alongside Millennials.

In grad school, I attempted to write a poetry manuscript filled with love poems to a generation. I dove into archival work that blurred the lines between memory and technology. And now I am doing this, an archive of the Millennial Epoch.

I don't really know what to say when people ask why I'm doing this or what for. People always want an end goal and all I want is to have fun.

Memory work is the most fun I've had. History, poetry, art, documentaries, technology. The things that make humans human. Yeah.
